value: Composition-versus-full Spearman rho = 0.988 over 21 library compounds at 1.0e-06 M.
Dropping the 6 compound(s) whose gain vector sits on the 0.05 floor leaves rho = 0.989: the correlation is not a tie artefact.

Reference 1 (arbitrary gain vectors, all gains moved at once): 50 draws of 21 vectors give rho median 0.808, 5th-95th percentile [0.615, 0.907]; the observed 0.988 is at the 100th percentile. Even compounds that do not exist, ordered by nothing but a shared random gain vector, reproduce most of the ordering.

Reference 2 (matched: one gain moved per pseudo-compound, the shape the shipped mechanism rules produce): rho median 0.847, 5th-95th percentile [0.676, 0.953] over 50 draws. The observed 0.988 is at the 100th percentile - above the reference range, but the reference median is already 0.847. A rank correlation of this size between levels B and D is therefore close to an algebraic identity: both are functions of the same gain vector, one through a fixed census and one through a row-normalised matrix whose cells average their presynaptic gains.

WHAT WOULD HAVE BEEN EVIDENCE AGAINST THE CLAIM that composition carries the ordering: an observed rho below the matched reference's 5th percentile (0.676), i.e. the census ordering the REAL library worse than it orders pseudo-compounds with no pharmacology in them. Evidence that the agreement was a substantive finding about this connectome would need the matched reference to sit well below the observed value - a median near zero, so that reproducing the ordering was a priori unlikely. Here the matched reference median is 0.847, so the quoted 0.99 should be read as the structural floor plus a small excess, not as a measurement of what the connectome contributes.

Shuffling the compound-to-gain assignment leaves rho = 0.988 against the observed 0.988 (difference +0). Both levels are functions of the gain vector alone, so a permutation of the labels moves the (B, D) pairs as a block and cannot change the rank correlation. The comparison therefore carries no compound-level information: it is a statement about the map from gains to readouts, not about which compound is which.

figures.name: F2_dual_scorecard.png
figures.caption: Dual scorecard for imidacloprid and fipronil at 1 µM. Bars are Hill occupancy of the insect target (blue) and its vertebrate counterpart (orange) for each of the five receptor pairs declared in `library.yaml:selectivity_pairs`. Hatched bars rest on a class placeholder: the compound has no sourced EC50 at that pair and the row is inert. Imidacloprid reaches 0.991 at insect nAChR against 0.091 at vertebrate a4b2; fipronil reaches 0.985 at insect RDL against 0.476 at native heteromeric vertebrate GABA-A. Teaching-tier EC50s: these are literature-order values, not measured constants.

figures.name: F11_evidence_types.png
figures.caption: What the compound library rests on, row by row. Left: the parameter each cited source actually measured. Middle: the ordered evidence distance between that source and this compound at this receptor in this species. Right: the transformation the type system then permits, which is a function of the two. Green marks the 10 on-target (E0) rows and the 1 of them that may use a physical binding-occupancy model; amber marks the proxy models, where the same Hill expression is computed but reported as a transfer with a warning naming the gap; red marks rows that carry no modellable evidence and return N/A rather than a small number. The type system, not a convention, enforces this: asking for an engagement from an untyped row raises rather than returning a value, and a soundness invariant is checked exhaustively over every row and every entry point.

figures.name: F3_occupancy_curves.png
figures.caption: Hill occupancy against free concentration for the four-compound panel, one insect target (solid, blue) and its vertebrate counterpart (dashed, orange) per compound. The shaded band is the selectivity window between the two EC50s, annotated in log10 units; the dotted vertical line is the 1 µM working concentration used elsewhere in the paper. Ivermectin's window is the GluCl/GlyR pair, deltamethrin's the Nav pair. Curves are the teaching library, not measured concentration-response data.

figures.name: F4_taste_motor_graph.png
figures.caption: Left: the committed MaleCNS v1.0 taste-motor cut (1841 cells, 19066 edges; 1 hop around MN9, DNp01 and the labellar GRN types, plus induced partner-partner edges of at least 10 synapses). Node and edge colour is the predicted consensus transmitter; layout is the deterministic superclass-column layout from `flylab.analysis.layout`. Seeds are marked: sweet GRNs (LB3b/c, up triangles), bitter GRNs (LB1a-d, down triangles), DNp01 (squares) and MN9 (stars). Right: the five strongest sweet and five strongest bitter paths of at most 3 synapses from a labellar GRN to MN9, ranked by the absolute product of signed synapse weights; there are 2595 such sweet and 2372 such bitter paths in total. The sweet/bitter assignment of LB types is a working hypothesis, not a MaleCNS annotation.

figures.name: F5_bitter_veto.png
figures.caption: MN9 firing on the map-extracted labellar-GRN path, driven through the real MaleCNS sweet (34) and bitter (38) GRN body IDs at 150 Hz, never by driving MN9 directly. Left: leaky rate engine. Right: Shiu-style LIF engine with a background Poisson drive. In vehicle, adding bitter drive takes MN9 to zero on both engines (veto ratio 0.00). Fipronil at 1 µM blocks RDL, raises the sugar-only rate and partially relieves the veto (ratio 0.41 rate, 0.16 LIF). Imidacloprid silences MN9 altogether, so its ratio is undefined rather than zero. Absolute rates differ between engines by construction and are not calibrated to any recording.

figures.name: F6_dependence_profile.png
figures.caption: Histograms are the drug effect (treated minus vehicle on the network mean rate) measured on 1000 degraded copies of the 1-hop MN9/DNp01 `named` cut; the red line is the same contrast on the real cut. Columns run in increasing order of destruction: transmitter labels permuted, synapse weights permuted, degree-preserving double-edge rewiring, Erdos-Renyi. Titles carry the empirical two-sided permutation p and the three-way verdict against the prespecified equivalence margin (delta = 0.332 Hz, 5 % of the vehicle readout): `distinguishable` means the test rejected, `equivalent within tolerance` means the gap from the null median is below the margin, and `indeterminate` means neither -- a failure to reject is not evidence that the degraded graph gives the same effect. Plain label permutation is shown because it is informative, but it moves the weighted excitation/inhibition balance as well as transmitter identity (T23), so it is a joint null and not a rung of the ladder. Imidacloprid is composition-dominated (necessary level: degree_sequence, equivalent_within_tolerance); fipronil is topology-dependent (necessary level: wiring_with_weighted_transmitter_balance).

figures.name: F12_dependence_landscape.png
figures.caption: Every compound of the library at four concentrations, on both committed cuts, classified by the weakest graph model the permutation test could **not** distinguish from the real cut -- never by a model that reproduces the effect. Classes are decided on Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted probabilities across each landscape's structural tests, with a prespecified relative effect floor of 1 % of the vehicle readout. Left, the 1-hop `named` cut: 11 of 84 cells need the wiring pattern, 42 are not distinguishable from any structure-preserving degradation, and 31 do not move the readout at all. Right, the denser `taste_motor` cut: 54 topology-dependent, 0 composition-dominated, 30 no-effect. The composition-dominated majority does not survive the change of substrate, and the `named` cut is an in-star whose degree-preserving rewire is close to the identity (T19).

figures.name: F16_instrument_validation.png
figures.caption: The dependence ladder pointed at a graph whose answer is known in advance. A recurrent cholinergic cycle of known strength is planted in a synthetic cut of the same size, density and transmitter composition as the `named` cut; a gain patch that collapses `g_ach` then removes an amplification that exists only while the cycle is intact, so the drug contrast depends on the wiring by construction. Left: the share of independently generated graphs the ladder classifies topology-dependent, against planted strength and permutation count. Right: the recovery experiment itself, with red marking the strengths the ladder recovered. The unplanted control is the empirical false-positive rate (0 of 18). Without this panel, a negative from the ladder would be indistinguishable from an under-powered test.

figures.name: F13_ablation.png
figures.caption: Each level predicts the same 21 compounds with one layer of information removed, and is scored by how well it reproduces the full model's *ordering* of the library (levels have different units, so values are not comparable; the correlation is signed, so a perfect inversion scores -1 rather than 1). Crosses mark the historical depression-only level-C rule, which applied a multiplier of at most 1.0 to every transmitter alike and so could not express disinhibition: its poor correlation was structural, not a finding about connectomes, and the conclusion drawn from it is withdrawn. With a direction-aware rule level C rises to 0.961 at 1 uM from 0.242. The composition level's agreement with the full model must be read against the matched reference distribution of T24, not on its own.

figures.name: F7_selectivity_landscape.png
figures.caption: Each point is one compound on one committed graph. The x axis is the receptor selectivity index from the library alone; the y axis is the circuit index, the log10 width of the window between the concentration that moves the simulated network mean rate by 50% and the concentration at which the most potent vertebrate target reaches 20% occupancy. Points below the dashed identity line are buffered by the circuit, points above are amplified. The split is by mechanism, not by potency: chlorpyrifos_oxon, ddt, deltamethrin, permethrin (Nav modulators and the AChE inhibitor) amplify, mean gap +0.29 log10 units, while the nAChR-acting set (acetamiprid, acetylcholine, clothianidin, imidacloprid, nicotine, nitenpyram) buffers, mean gap -0.87. Compounds with no circuit index (chlordimeform, dieldrin, fipronil, gaba, ivermectin, picrotoxin, spinosad, sulfoxaflor, thiamethoxam) never reach the 50% threshold on this cut and are omitted.

figures.name: F8_dose_response_sensitivity.png
figures.caption: Left: the model's own dose-response for imidacloprid on the 1-hop MN9/DNp01 cut. Points are 4 replicates per concentration with log-normal EC50 jitter (sd 0.3 log10 units) and drive jitter; the curve is a 4-parameter Hill fit, and the band is a 200-resample bootstrap CI on the fitted IC50 (34.7 nM). This is the *model's* circuit IC50, not a receptor IC50 and not an animal IC50. Right: one-at-a-time sensitivity of the same readout at 1 µM, each parameter halved and doubled. The gain-rule coefficient dominates; the EC50 and Hill coefficient have zero span because occupancy is already saturated at this dose.

figures.name: F9_genotype_panel.png
figures.caption: Target-receptor occupancy at 1 uM for wild type and each published resistance allele that has a sourced fold-shift for that compound. Grey bars are alleles with no sourced number for the compound: they are left identical to wild type and reported, never extrapolated. Left and centre: fipronil and imidacloprid. Right: the specificity check that motivates the per-compound rule. *para* M918T (super-kdr) shifts deltamethrin 100-fold but leaves DDT at 1-fold, and *Rdl* A301S shifts GABA 33.9-fold while leaving fipronil at 1.1-fold. A toggle that shifted a whole receptor uniformly would be wrong in both cases.

figures.name: F10_rank_validation.png
figures.caption: Left: the model's compound ordering against each published ordering that the teaching library can cover, with Spearman's rho per entry and the number of compounds it orders. 8 entry-assay combinations are evaluable and 16 are skipped because the library cannot cover them; 4 of the evaluable ones order exactly two compounds, where rho can only be +-1, so no bare mean is quoted: over the 4 entries with more than two compounds the mean is 0.756, and as a concordance count the result is 8 concordant against 0 discordant orderings (two-sided binomial p = 0.008). Right: the two inversions the validation module records rather than fixes. Nitenpyram sits near the top of the library's insect nAChR potency ordering and is the least potent neonicotinoid in *Drosophila* whole-animal bioassays, and clothianidin/imidacloprid are ordered the opposite way from the bioassays. Both are receptor-EC50 versus whole-animal-potency differences: the whole-animal number contains uptake, penetration and metabolism, which FlyLab does not model.

figures.name: F14_conclusion_stability.png
figures.caption: Each row is a conclusion this paper could state; each column is one prespecified, admissible way of turning receptor engagement into synaptic gain. Green retains the conclusion, red reverses it, amber means the readout does not exist under that specification. The topology rows are decided on 100 permutations per specification and on Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted probabilities across the 100 structural tests of the run; until v0.6.1 the specification never reached the engine those rows were computed on, so their uniformity was guaranteed by construction rather than measured. Retained by every specification: C2_rdl_disinhibition, C3_imidacloprid_topology_not_distinguishable, C4_fipronil_topology_exceeds, C7_map_bitter_veto. The nicotinic suppression conclusion is reversed by every monotone rule, which is how a result that depends on a modelling choice looks when it is tested rather than asserted; and for a conclusion shaped as a failure to reject, the fraction retained is only as strong as the equivalence behind it (T14's `n_equivalent_within_tolerance` against `n_indeterminate`).

figures.name: F15_uncertainty_voi.png
figures.caption: Left: the share of the variance of the neighbourhood mean rate attributable to each assumption, first-order and total-order, from a Saltelli cross-sample with Jansen estimators, with bootstrap first-order confidence intervals. A factor is **resolved** only when its interval excludes zero; the starred rows are not, and a factor's index exceeding the noise floor does not resolve it. The dashed line is that floor, defined as the largest magnitude among the *negative* first-order estimates: a true first-order index cannot be negative, so that magnitude is a measured lower bound on the estimator's error, and on this run it is several times the declared null factor's own draw (0.046 set by gain_coef, against lif_seed at -0.007). Right: the same shares scaled back into the readout's variance and mapped onto the experiment that would resolve each assumption; a negative estimate is clipped to zero for the decision value, because a value of information cannot be negative. Green marks a factor that needs no experiment at all, only a re-analysis of data already held.

figures.name: F1_architecture.png
figures.caption: FlyLab dataflow. A compound and a free concentration enter the occupancy engine, which reads the sourced library (optionally shifted by a genotype, combined with a mixture partner, or driven by an exposure profile). Occupancy splits into two scorecards. The insect side passes through the mechanism table to a gain patch on transmitter classes of a named MaleCNS cut; the vertebrate side is scored at the same dose and never touches a circuit. The circuit runtime (rate or LIF) produces named-cell readouts, which the analysis and validation layers turn into empirical permutation probabilities with their three-way verdicts, selectivity indices, rank correlations and prospective predictions. Everything lands in one notebook JSON with a provenance block.

notes: [mechanisms] 5 of the 7 transmitter sign magnitudes the rate engine iterates (glutamate -0.4, histamine -0.5, dopamine +0.2, serotonin +0.2, octopamine +0.2) are asserted rather than measured, are exempt from the specification family and are not bounded by the label-permuting null. They are now published in T21 rather than left in the source.

[graph] the `named` cut is an in-star: 85% of its 1360 edges terminate on its 4 seed cells, only 184 of 1126 nodes receive any input and only 25% of edges leave a node that itself receives input (mean degree 1.21). A degree-preserving rewire of such a graph is close to the identity, so a negative topology verdict on this cut is weak evidence. The `taste_motor` cut (mean degree 10.36) is the substrate to generalise from.

[graph] the `named` cut contains no octopaminergic cell at all, so a compound whose only insect mechanism acts through g_oct (chlordimeform) cannot move this readout for substrate reasons rather than pharmacological ones.

[veto] imidacloprid at 1 uM silences MN9 on the map path on both engines (sugar-driven MN9 = 0 Hz), so its bitter-veto ratio is undefined, not 0. g_ach hits the 0.05 floor, which removes the cholinergic GRN->MN9 drive itself. This is a property of the agonist patch rule, and it is why the taste-map arm of the null panel is undefined for imidacloprid.

[dependence] the transmitter null matters to the equivalence claim and not to the probability: imidacloprid's gap from the null median is 2.65 Hz under the plain label permutation and 0.24 Hz under the weight-matched null, against a prespecified margin of 0.332 Hz. The plain permutation is a joint target-set-and-sign null and is reported as one.

[dependence] the fipronil bitter-veto ratio on the taste-motor path is a negative at n=300 shuffles (max |z| = 0.220, p resolution 0.0033): the veto ratio is model behaviour, not evidence about the wiring, and the verdicts say which modes are equivalent within tolerance (none) and which are merely indeterminate (erdos_renyi, rewire_degree_preserving, sign_permute, sign_permute_weight_matched, weight_permute).

[dependence] plain transmitter-label permutation does NOT preserve the weighted excitation/inhibition balance: the cholinergic share of total outgoing synaptic weight is 0.619 on the real `named` cut against 0.544 +- 0.027 over 1000 permutations, putting the real graph at the 100th percentile of its own null. The weight-matched null holds every tracked share within 0.002.

[dependence] instrument validation: the ladder recovered 2 of 3 planted topology-dependent effects at n = 200 and returned no false positive on the unplanted control. Detection over the planted grid by permutation count is n=50: 0.61, n=200: 0.61, n=1000: 0.67 and by planted strength strength 0.25: 0.00-0.17; strength 0.5: 0.67-0.83; strength 1: 1.00-1.00; the empirical false-positive rate on the unplanted control is 0 of 18. Effect size dominates the permutation count: full power at planted strength 1, detection at or below one in four at 0.25.

[dependence] multiplicity changes the headline count on the `named` cut: 14 cells are topology-dependent on the raw permutation p and 11 survive Benjamini-Hochberg across the 168 structural tests of the landscape. The corrected count is the one the paper quotes.

[dependence] the central RQ2 result REVERSES on a cut that has topology: repeated on `taste_motor` (1841 nodes, 19066 edges, mean degree 10.4) the landscape returns 0 composition-dominated cells of 84, against 42 of 84 on the in-star `named` cut. The composition-dominated majority is a property of the substrate, not of receptor perturbation on connectomes.

[ablation] the ablation ladder's ranking is concentration-dependent: with the historical depression-only level-C rule the weakest level is 10 nM: C_topology_only; 100 nM: A_receptor_only; 1 µM: A_receptor_only; 10 µM: A_receptor_only. Any sentence of the form 'the topology-only level is the worst of the four' is true of one column and false of the others.

[ablation] the level-C conclusion is withdrawn: with a direction-aware generic rule the topology-only baseline's rank correlation with the full model at 1 uM rises from 0.242 (depression-only floor, which cannot express disinhibition and whose every entry is at most zero) to 0.961. 'The connectome without the pharmacology is not a cheap substitute' was a statement about a sign-broken baseline.

[ablation] the composition-versus-full correlation carries no compound-level information: shuffling the compound-to-gain assignment leaves it identically 0.988, and pharmacology-free pseudo-compounds whose gain vectors have the shape the mechanism rules produce already reach a median of 0.847. Both levels are functions of the same gain vector, so the number is a statement about the map from gains to readouts.

[ablation] the composition verdict is not robust to the engine's row normalisation: the B-versus-D rank correlation at 1 uM is 0.988 under the shipped `row_abs` mode and 0.666 under a degree-corrected one. The normalisation is an undocumented modelling choice that makes each cell's recurrent input a composition-weighted average of its presynaptic gains.

[landscape] no circuit selectivity index exists for chlordimeform, dieldrin, fipronil, gaba, ivermectin, picrotoxin, spinosad, sulfoxaflor, thiamethoxam: on this neighbourhood their largest relative change in the mean rate never reaches the 50% threshold (RDL/GluCl blockers are bounded by the GABA/glutamate share of the cut and by the 0.05 gain floor).

[dose] at 1 uM imidacloprid the model is exactly insensitive to a 2x change in the insect_nAChR EC50 and in the Hill coefficient (span 0 Hz): occupancy is saturated, so the gain-rule coefficient is the only parameter that still moves the readout. A dose-response experiment, not a single high dose, is what constrains the EC50.

[validation] the literature-concordance mean is not quotable bare: 4 of the 8 evaluable comparisons order exactly two compounds, where Spearman's rho can only be +-1 and the two-sided p is 1.0 whatever the model does. Over the 4 comparisons with more than two compounds the mean is 0.756; as a concordance count it is 8 concordant against 0 discordant orderings (two-sided binomial p = 0.008).

[stability] the C3 retention rate is no longer vacuous and is no longer uniform: at n_shuffles = 100 (resolution 0.0099, against the previous 6 at which p <= 0.05 was arithmetically unattainable) the conclusion is retained by 25 of 25 specifications, but only 17 of those reach equivalence within the prespecified margin; 8 are merely indeterminate.

[stability] the suppression conclusion is specification-dependent: 10 of 25 prespecified specifications reverse it. Under linear@1.00x the same compound at the same engagement EXCITES the network (10.1 Hz treated vs 6.631 Hz vehicle) instead of suppressing it. Suppression is a property of the biphasic desensitisation term, not of the pharmacology-connectome integration.

[stability] the supplement's claim that the monotone rules 'buffer at least as much, never less' is false: 3 of the 6 reversing specifications with a defined index buffer LESS than the shipped rule (linear@1.50x, saturating@1.25x, saturating@1.50x), and the aggregate of -0.893 is carried by the extreme of a range running -0.199 to -1.734.

[stability] T8 and T15 have different scopes and must be read that way: T8 scores the whole library on both cuts, T15 only the 10 compounds of the two mechanism classes the conclusion is about. acetylcholine carries a circuit index in T8 and is outside T15's compound set entirely.

[stability] the amplify/buffer split is NOT stable across the 3x3 threshold grid: nav_ache fails at circuit_frac=0.50,vert_limit=0.10. The paper quotes the range over the grid, never the point estimate.

[uncertainty] the estimator's noise floor is 0.046, set by the most negative first-order estimate (gain_coef), not by the declared null factor lif_seed at -0.007. Only gain_transform, weight_threshold have a first-order confidence interval that excludes zero; every other factor is unresolved at this sample size, and a negative point estimate is estimator error rather than a negative contribution.

[claims] the provenance chain behind a circuit readout has 9 links and exactly 1 of them (malecns_edges) is a measurement of the system being simulated; the rest are literature reuse, asserted modelling choices and computation.

[scale] scale study: 7 cuts (scale_1k, named, taste_motor, scale_5k, scale_10k, scale_25k, scale_50k); verdicts settled on the clean ladder: yes. imidacloprid: the verdict is 'topology-dependent' on the largest 5 of 7 cuts tested, first reached at 'taste_motor'. fipronil: the verdict is 'topology-dependent' on the largest 7 of 7 cuts tested, first reached at 'scale_1k'.
honesty: Every number in this file is model_derived: it comes from the teaching EC50 library, the gain patch rules and one or two hops-limited MaleCNS cuts. Nothing here was measured in a living fly.
live_lab is null in every notebook this pipeline produced.
--fast reduces replicate and shuffle counts only; z-scores and CIs from a fast run are noisier than the paper's.
